newsitem.title: INDIA: Hindu party leader gets bail in rioting case.
newsitem.headline: Hindu party leader gets bail in rioting case.

text.p: Bal Thackeray, the firebrand chief of India's regional Hindu Shiv Sena party, was granted bail by a Bombay judge on Monday in a five-year-old case of rioting.
Eyewitnesses said Thackeray, dressed in traditional Indian tunic and tight trousers, seemed subdued as the judge granted him bail and excused him from attending hearings personally.
Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate K.H. Holambe-Patil told a crowded courtroom he had directed Thackeray's lawyers to ensure he came to the court to face the charges against him.
Thackeray, who sat in a rickety chair with no back in the front row, had earlier smiled and waved to journalists as he made his way to the courtroom in Bandra, a northwestern suburb.
Thackeray's lawyer said he paid 5,000 rupees ($139) as bail in a 1991 rioting case in which members of Shiv Sena (Army of Shiva) ransacked the offices of "Mahanagar", a local newspaper.

The newspaper had criticised Thackeray's opposition to the staging of the India-Pakistan World Cup cricket match in Bombay, cancelled after Shiv Sena members poured oil and tar on the pitch at Bombay's Wankhede stadium.
On October 25, 1991, angry Shiv Sena members rampaged through the "Mahanagar" newsroom, destroying equipment and assaulting two of the staff.

Thackeray opposed the match because he accused Islamabad of fomenting violence in Kashmir, hotly disputed by both India and Pakistan, which have fought two of their three wars over it since independence from Britain in 1947.

Police have named Thackeray as the main accused in the case, and charged him with inciting his party members to violence. India's legal system, plagued by lengthy delays, has only recently begun hearing the case.
On Tuesday, the same judge will begin hearing a motion by the Maharashtra state government to drop the case against Thackeray, who rules his party like an autocrat but has never stood for election.
The Shiv Sena rules India's wealthiest state of Maharashtra in coalition with the national opposition Bharatiya Janata Party. The coalition took power in March 1995.
The case against Thackeray was filed by the previous Congress state government.
